info.name: STRIKE API
info.description:
API collection for STRIKE, the cross-border pricing/quoting engine. Import the accompanying "STRIKE - Local" environment alongside this collection and select it before sending requests.

There is no public registration endpoint — accounts are created by an admin (eventually via the admin dashboard; for now, run `node ace create:user` in apps/server to create a login for testing this collection).

request.description:
Logs in an existing user with email + password. Returns the user's public info and a new bearer token valid for 30 days.

Fails with 400 for an unknown email or an incorrect password (same error either way, so it can't be used to discover registered emails).

Returns the currently authenticated user, identified by the bearer token saved from Login.

Fails with 401 if the token is missing, invalid, or has been logged out.
Read-only lookup data seeded from the old project's reference tables. Similar endpoints exist for /reference/regions, /currencies, /use-cases, /integration-types, and /icp-nodes.
The master corridor catalog a user picks from when adding a corridor to a quote. Supports optional ?countryId=&serviceCode=&transactionTypeCode= filters.

query.description: true to exclude any payer containing "swift wire transfer" from every count
true to restrict the whole picker to the old app's compliance country allow-list (mirrors selecting "Last Mile Payout"/"Account Top-Up" as a use case)

request.description: Powers the "Corridors to Offer" picker: per-dimension counts (regions, countries, services, transaction types, payout currencies, payers) plus totalAvailable/totalMatched, given any combination of the query filters. Every dimension supports multiple selected values (comma-separated, OR within a dimension, AND across dimensions). Region is a one-way filter: it narrows every other dimension but is never itself narrowed, even by its own filter — the other five dimensions narrow each other mutually (never by their own filter). Every panel always lists every value that exists, even ones with count 0, so the UI can disable rather than remove them.

Creates a new quote, owned by the current user, always starting in 'draft' status.

Most fields are optional besides name — this example shows the multi-value ones (a quote can have several funding/source currencies and use cases, matching the old app exactly). Other optional fields: partnerCountryId, integrationTypeId, icpLevel1Id/icpLevel2Id/icpLevel3Id, contractLengthYears, waivedMonths, partnerPrCode, showFxSourceInContract, showFxSpreadInContract, fxModel, selectedPricingStrategy, selectedFxPricing, defaultFeeCurrencyId. Currency/use-case ids depend on what's seeded — check "List Countries"/"Currencies" first if these don't exist in your database.
Lists the current user's own quotes (an admin sees every quote).
Returns the full quote (with its corridors) plus backend-computed totals (revenue, margin, take rate) — the client never computes these itself.
Only allowed while the quote is still in 'draft' status — fails with 409 once submitted.

Adds a corridor from the catalog to the quote. The backend computes revenue/FX margin/margin fee/gross margin/take-rate using the corridor's real cost/FX-source master data, and flags approval via two independent checks: needs_financial_approval (margin/pricing rules, with financial_approval_reasons) and needs_network_approval (a lookup on the corridor catalog's own Need Approval/Internal/Central Bank fields, with network_approval_reasons) — needs_approval/approval_reasons remain the combined OR of both for backward compatibility. None of this is trusted from the request body. Run "List Corridors (catalog)" first to populate {{corridor_id}}.

Updates pricing inputs for a corridor already on the quote — the backend recomputes revenue/FX margin/margin fee/gross margin/take-rate and both approval checks (financial + network, see "Add Corridor to Quote") from the merged values.

Returns `{ setupFee: null }` until the tab has been saved once, otherwise `{ setupFee: {...} }` with every backend-computed value (finalCommitmentFee, year1CommittedRevenue, totalContractValue, needsApproval, approvalReasons) plus its milestones/principal-slots/block-fees/other-fees.

  "quotedPrice": 100000,

  "standardCommitmentFee": 5000,
  "commitmentFeeDiscountPct": 0,

  "rebateIncentive": false,
  "otherFees": [

    { "conceptCode": "proof_of_payment", "amount": 10, "isPercentage": false },
    { "conceptCode": "emergency_funding", "amount": 0.3, "isPercentage": true },

}

request.description: Creates or replaces the quote's whole Setup Fee tab in one call (only allowed while the quote is in 'draft' status). The backend validates cross-field consistency (custom payment milestones must sum to exactly 100%, principal-based MCF must have enough slots for the contract length, waived months capped at 6 — the old app's own UI never actually allowed past 6 despite its input saying 24) and computes finalCommitmentFee/year1CommittedRevenue/totalContractValue/needsApproval/approvalReasons itself — none of that is trusted from the request body. otherFees concept codes: reversal_request, proof_of_payment, emergency_funding, treasury_management, business_hub_platform, post_funding_penalty, corridor_no_usage, white_glove, stablecoin_prefunding, digital_asset_icp_setup, bulk_currency_conversion, currencies_for_treasury. For a custom payment schedule, add a paymentMilestones array; for a principal-based MCF, add mcfPrincipalSlots (2 slots for a 12-month contract, 3 for longer).
Only allowed while the quote is still in 'draft' status.

Revokes the current bearer token. Deliberately placed last in the collection — every other request needs the token, so logging out too early breaks everything after it. Run this manually whenever you're done, don't rely on "Run collection" order alone unless this folder truly runs last.
